reconcile.note: Henry distinguishes Jesus's silence toward the chief priests' false accusations from his direct answer to Pilate's own question, which corresponds to John's fuller dialogue.

discrepancy.note: Strauss observes Matthew and Mark leave Jesus's silence before Pilate unexplained, a gap he says only John's fuller dialogue clears up.

quotes.text: In Matthew and Mark, it is true, to the affirmation of Jesus that he is the king of the Jews is added his silence, in opposition to the manifold accusations of the Sanhedrists—a silence which surprises Pilate … On the other hand, this point is sufficiently clear in the fourth gospel.
quotes.attr: David Friedrich Strauss (d. 1874), The Life of Jesus Critically Examined (1846), on Matthew 27:14 and John 18:37.

sides.snippet: He gave him no answer, not even one word, so that the governor marveled greatly.

sides.verseText: Pilate therefore said to him, \"Are you a king then?\" Jesus answered, \"You say that I am a king. For this reason I have been born, and for this reason I have come into the world, that I should testify to the truth. Everyone who is of the truth listens to my voice.\"
